status_summary: The text presumes continued US participation in multilateral health bodies, with an appointee coordinating accountability from within and more prominent US representation on technical and standard-setting bodies; the government instead exited. The US completed withdrawal from the WHO on 2026-01-22 under Executive Order 14155, ending funding and withdrawing all US personnel, rejected the 2024 International Health Regulations amendments on 2025-07-18, and a memorandum of 2026-01-07 directed withdrawal from 66 organizations including UNFPA and UN Women. Some steps align in part with the accountability and abortion-language elements: State withheld FY2025 UNFPA funding under the Kemp-Kasten amendment on 2025-05-08, the Protecting Life in Foreign Assistance rule (2026-01-27) applies abortion-related award terms to public international organizations, and HHS and State said on 2026-08-12 the US would host the Geneva Consensus Declaration secretariat, one of whose objectives is work across the UN system. Because the representation element ran opposite to the text and no appointee coordinator was found, the record is judged diverged.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14155 directed US withdrawal from the World Health Organization.
The administration invoked the Kemp-Kasten amendment to withhold FY2025 UNFPA funding, expected to total about $32.5 million in core support.
HHS and State announced the US rejection of the 2024 amendments to the International Health Regulations.
A think-tank analysis described the America First Global Health Strategy, which shifts health aid to bilateral agreements.
A presidential memorandum of 2026-01-07 directed withdrawal from 66 international organizations, conventions and treaties, including UNFPA and UN Women.
HHS and State announced completion of the WHO withdrawal, with US funding ended, all US personnel withdrawn and activities shifted to direct bilateral engagement.
State published the Protecting Life in Foreign Assistance final rule, extending abortion-related award terms to international organizations and foreign governments.
AFP, via La Libre, reported a senator's statement that the US would provide $600 million in congressionally appropriated funds to Gavi, which the administration had stopped in June 2025.
HHS and State said the US would take over the Secretariat of the Geneva Consensus Declaration, which has an objective of working across the UN system.

title: Hold the UN, WHO and other multilateral partners to account from within
uncertainties: No source was found showing US statements or negotiating positions at the UN in 2025 or 2026 seeking removal of abortion-related language from documents; the researcher's searches and one reviewer search returned only 2018 and 2019 coverage. The KFF explainer was published 2026-04-17 and gives the 2025-05-08 event date. The Gavi item rests on an AFP report relaying a senator's written statement and was not confirmed against a State or Senate source; it describes the funds as provided by the US, not a State commitment. Whether any political appointee holds a coordination role is unknown. The stage is a judgment call: the funding conditions and the Geneva Consensus role could support in_progress at about 15 on the accountability element, but the text's premise of working from within and expanding representation was reversed. Withdrawal from international organizations aligns with a different recommendation in the State chapter, tracked in c06-03.
